#en:
I am writing this in the back booth of a cheap bar in Neon, because the station noise is the only thing loud enough to drown out that story people keep telling.

It started as a freight joke a couple years back, just something haulers tossed around when a run was late. A Trade Authority courier takes a contract off some no-name rock, cuts a new lane, never shows on the main traffic boards again. First time I heard it, the ship was small, the jump short, the pilot greedy. Next time, it was a larger freighter, different system, heroic captain chasing a shortcut. Now, depending who is drinking, you get Crimson Fleet ambushes, UC coverups, cursed coordinates, or a ghost in the nav.

Every retelling adds a detail, sands off another. Sometimes they mention a woman who can thread a jump through the width of a needle, sometimes she is just a rumor tacked on at the end. Nobody agrees on where the route started or ended, but the shape of it stays the same, a line that goes somewhere it should not.

I used to laugh it off. Lately I notice people lower their voices when they reach the part about missing ships. I have seen the way certain captains flinch when an extra route segment shows up on their charts, unasked for. The facts are thin as vacuum, but the fear is thick, and fear has a way of rewriting the map long before anyone sees what really waits at the edge.
zh:
我在霓虹城一间廉价酒吧的后排卡座里写下这些，因为这空间站的噪声是唯一响到能盖过那个故事的东西。

它两年前还是一句货运笑话，不过是运货船员在航次晚了时随口念叨的东西。一艘贸易管理局快船从某块无名岩石上接了份合同，开出一条新航道，从此再没出现在主交通板上。我第一次听到时，那艘船很小，跃迁很短，飞行员很贪。下次听到时，它变成了一艘更大的货船、另一个星系、一位追逐捷径的英雄船长。如今，取决于谁在喝酒，你会听到深红舰队的伏击、联殖的掩盖、被诅咒的坐标，或者导航里闹鬼。

每次转述都会添一个细节、磨掉另一个。有时他们提到一个女人，能把一次跃迁穿过针眼般的宽度；有时她只是结尾处钉上去的一则传言。没人对这条航线从哪里开始、到哪里结束意见一致，可它的形状始终如一：一条通往它不该去之处的线。

我以前一笑置之。近来我注意到，人们讲到失踪飞船那部分时会压低声音。我见过某些船长在星图上无缘无故多出一段航线时的畏缩。事实薄如真空，恐惧却厚实，而恐惧有一种本事，能在任何人看清边缘究竟等着什么之前，就先改写地图。

#en:
I started taking the "special" routes because they were easy credits.

First it was just a five-minute offset on a run out of Gagarin. The controller on the line sounded bored, professional, and the corridor he slid us into was clean as glass. No pirates, no traffic, no questions from anyone in Trade Authority when the manifest closed out. Then it became ten minutes here, twenty there, little nudges around Navy patrols and busy lanes, always accompanied by a quiet assurance that the windows were safe and well-compensated.

I did not notice when the voice on the other end stopped reading from standard tables and started anticipating our fuel load, our usual speed, the way our captain likes to cut burn. I did not mind when a few of our delivery times stopped matching the official charts, as long as the bonuses kept posting and no one from the Hub asked why our logs looked cleaner than everyone else's.

Now there is a Navy scout floating cold out where our last "adjustment" led, and a courier like mine has gone dark with its holds still full. People say it is coincidence, that routes shift every day and only the unlucky get caught in the gaps. But when I listen back to the old comms, to that calm voice telling me we are "just inside the safe window," all I can hear are the hundreds of little yeses I whispered to myself, lining up in a row I never meant to draw.
zh:
我开始接那些"特殊"航线，因为那是轻松钱。

起初只是从加加林一趟航次上五分钟的错峰。线路那头的管制员听起来很无聊、很专业，他给我们滑进去的走廊干净得像玻璃。没有海盗，没有交通，清单结清时贸易管理局也没人问一句。后来就变成这里十分钟、那里二十分钟，一些绕着海军巡逻和繁忙航道的小小轻推，每次总伴随着一句安静的保证：时窗安全，报酬丰厚。

我没注意到另一头那个声音是什么时候不再照着标准表念、而开始预判我们的燃料负载、惯常速度、以及我们船长喜欢怎么削减点火。我也没在意我们的一些送达时间什么时候开始和官方星图对不上，只要奖金照发、枢纽那边没人问为什么我们的日志比别人的都干净就行。

如今，我们最后一次"调整"所通向的地方，冷冰冰地漂着一艘海军侦察艇；而一艘像我这样的快船也陷入了沉寂，货舱还满着。人们说这是巧合，说航线每天都变，只有倒霉的才被夹在缝隙里。可当我回听那些旧通讯，回听那个平静的声音告诉我们"刚好在安全时窗内"时，我听到的全是我对自己悄声说过的成百上千个"好"，排成一行我从未打算画出的线。

#en:
I snuck back to the bunker again after shift, even though they have taped half the doors and killed the main grid. The place hums anyway, like it remembers being useful. I jacked into the auxiliary and pulled the last week of atmospheric scans before shutdown. There it was, buried under routine traffic and supply flights and some smuggler who thought his heat profile looked like a mining shuttle. One thread that did not match any filed route, skimming the edge of restricted airspace, slipping in and out between pulses like it knew when the grid blinked.

The signature is subtle, but it repeats with the same timing as those anomaly reports everyone pretends they have never read. It angles away from the usual traffic lanes, then climbs hard toward that research spire they built out past the old farms, the one nobody talks about unless the doors are shut and the volume is low. In the mess, when the conversation drifts that way, people joke about "ghost inspectors" and change the subject quick, eyes on the corners like sound might carry farther than it should.  

Out on that lonely rock, where the first cache turned up, the gaps in the satellite recorder bothered me. The half-scrubbed safety audit from New Atlantis bothered me more. Now this flight path ties both to the same tower of glass and sealed labs, and I am starting to think none of this is random malfunction.
zh:
交班后我又溜回了碉堡，尽管他们用胶带封了一半的门、切断了主电网。这地方居然还在嗡鸣，像它记得自己曾被派过用场。我接进辅助系统，调出关闭前最后一周的大气扫描。它就在那儿，埋在例行交通、补给航班，和一个自以为热量特征像采矿穿梭机的走私贩底下。一条不属于任何申报航线的线索，贴着受限空域的边缘掠过，在一次次的脉冲之间忽进忽出，像它知道电网什么时候眨眼。

那特征很细微，可它重复的时序和那些人人都假装从没读过的异常报告一致。它偏离惯常交通航道，然后费力地朝旧农场外那座研究尖塔爬去——那座除非门窗紧闭、音量压低，没人会谈起的研究尖塔。在食堂里，当话题飘向那个方向时，人们会拿"幽灵检查员"开玩笑，然后飞快换话题，眼睛盯着每个角落，像声音可能传得比它该传的更远。

在那块孤独的岩石上，也就是第一个缓存被发现的地方，卫星记录仪里的空白让我不安。来自新亚特兰蒂斯那份被擦了一半的安全审计更让我不安。如今这条飞行路径把两者都系到了同一座玻璃与密封实验室的尖塔上，我开始觉得这一切都不是随机故障。

#en:
Personal log, unsent

I signed onto WK-9192 because I thought flying with SysDef meant clear lines: good ships, bad ships, and us in between. Turns out most of the time it is spreadsheets in vacuum. Patrol the same corridors, trust the same relays, let the traffic flow like it always has. Somewhere along the way, we stopped asking why the routes bent the way they do.

Lately the bends are sharper.

The last update from command pushed us closer to that dead relay chain, and nobody blinked. Nav just folded the new vectors in. I watched the model spin and, for a second, it looked like someone had reached in and dragged the whole pattern sideways with a fingertip. The numbers still balanced, so no one cared.

Back on that drop shelter a few weeks ago, a Fleet liaison swore their smuggling runs were arriving early without extra burn. I chalked it up to bravado and bad accounting. Now I see the same tiny discrepancies ghosting through our own logs, the same improbable timing, the same gaps where patrols should be. Different ships, different factions, one invisible hand nudging everyone toward the quiet spots between signals.

Feels like the lanes made their choice before any of us did, and we just kept following the glow on the console. If there is someone out there rewriting the map, we have been sailing along their ink the whole time, pretending the tide is natural.
zh:
个人日志，未发送

我签上 WK-9192，是因为我以为随联殖防务飞行意味着界线分明：好船、坏船，以及夹在中间的我们。结果大多数时候它只是真空里的电子表格。巡逻同样的走廊，信任同样的中继站，让交通像一直以来的那样流动。一路上不知何时，我们不再追问那些航线为什么会那样弯。

近来弯得更急。

指挥部上一次更新把我们推得离那条死掉的中继链更近，而没人眨眼。导航只是把新矢量折了进去。我看着模型旋转，有那么一瞬间，它看起来像有人伸进来用指尖把整个图案朝旁边拖了一下。数字仍然平衡，所以没人在意。

几周前在那个空投掩体里，一名舰队联络员赌咒说他们的走私航次没有额外点火就提前抵达了。我当时把它归为吹牛和记账太烂。如今我在我们自己的日志里也看到同样微小的出入在游荡，同样不可能的时序，同样在巡逻该在处的空白。不同的飞船、不同的派系，一只看不见的手把所有人推向信号之间的安静角落。

感觉这些航道在我们任何人做出选择之前就先做了选择，而我们只是不断跟着控制台上的那点光。要是外面真有人在改写地图，那我们从一开始就是沿着他的墨迹航行，假装那潮水是天生的。

#en:
I took this post because I thought it would be quiet.

End of the lane, moonside, nothing but rock dust in the vents and haulers too tired to argue about docking fees. You pour them a drink, bump their escort requirement down one ship, look the other way on a crate or two, and everyone goes home a little richer. That is how the clerk before me explained it, anyway, right before he shipped out on a transfer he did not deserve.

I have been going through his old logs, trying to make sense of the routing overrides he left half-finished. Same pattern keeps blinking back at me. Convoys pushed a little off the standard corridor, insurance coverages quietly adjusted, all flagged with an internal tag I cannot clear, like some ghost auditor riding shotgun on every change.

At first I figured it was some automated safety routine, overzealous system guarding cargo values. Then I noticed the dates lining up with raids you hear about in bar talk: that HopeTech freighter that never made its refuel, the Narion runs that "just disappeared" between beacons. Tiny edits, over and over, and everyone who touched them already rotated to better posts, patting themselves on the back for a few extra credits.

I cannot say what any of it means yet. All I know is somebody smart set this in motion a long time ago, and the rest of us have been pressing confirm without ever seeing the whole board.
zh:
我接下这个岗位，是因为我以为它会很安静。

航道尽头，卫星背阴面，通风口里只有岩尘，运货船员累得懒得为停靠费争吵。你给他们倒杯酒，把他们的护航要求降掉一艘船，对一两只货箱睁只眼闭只眼，大家就都富一点点地回家。至少我前面那个文员是这么解释的——就在他搭上一趟他并不配得到的调任之前。

我一直在翻他留下的旧日志，想弄明白那些他做了一半的航路越权改动。同一个图案不断朝我眨眼。运输队被稍微推离标准走廊，保险覆盖被悄悄调整，全都带着一个我无法清除的内部标记，像有个幽灵审计员在每一次改动上搭顺风车。

起初我以为那是某种自动安全例行程序，一个过于尽责、守护货物价值的系统。后来我注意到那些日期与酒吧闲谈里听到的劫案对得上：那艘从未完成补给的霍普科技货船，"在信标之间突然消失"的纳里昂航次。一次又一次微小的编辑，而每个碰过它们的人都已经轮换到更好的岗位，为多挣的几个信用币自我夸赞。

我还说不清这一切意味着什么。我只知道很久以前有个聪明人启动了它，而我们其余人一直在按"确认"键，却从未见过整块棋盘。

#en:
It started as background noise. Little things the settlers tacked onto their complaints about broken pumps and missed supply drops. A hauler swore his escort peeled away just as the sky went white and somehow his ship rode the worst of it without a scratch. A mining foreman mentioned a quiet woman in a battered flight jacket who spent more time staring at the clouds than at her drink. At first I filed it under frontier exaggeration. Then the coordinates started to line up.

I keep a private overlay, separate from the reports I send up the chain. Storm incidents, convoy disappearances, odd sensor gaps. They were scattered across systems that have nothing in common except a habit of bad weather and neglect. But when I plotted the approach vectors people described, I started seeing the same thin corridor traced over and over, like someone was sewing through storms with the same needle.

The last batch of logs did it for me. Three separate captains, weeks apart, all mentioned ghost traffic in the same sector, right before their feeds went to static. One of them caught a partial transponder, old UC formatting, tagged to a long-range combat hull that is supposed to be mothballed. That is not the kind of coincidence you shrug off. Whatever she is doing out there, she is riding routes we built and buried, and the next step sits on a dead Navy ship that has no business being where it is.
zh:
它起初只是背景噪声。是定居者们在关于坏掉的泵和错过的补给投递的抱怨上附带的小事。一个运货船员赌咒说他的护航船在天变白的那一刻正好脱离，而他的船不知怎的闯过了最糟的部分却毫发无伤。一个矿场工头提到一个穿着破旧飞行夹克、安静的女人，盯着云的时间比盯着自己酒杯的时间还长。起初我把它归进边疆夸大之词。后来那些坐标开始对上了。

我私下留了一份叠加图，和我上报给链条的报告分开。风暴事件、运输队失踪、古怪的传感器空白。它们散落在彼此毫无共同点的星系里——除了都惯有恶劣天气和疏于管理。可当我把人们描述的进近矢量标绘出来时，我开始看见同一条细窄的走廊被一遍遍描过，像有人用同一根针在风暴中缝纫。

最后一批日志让我彻底信了。三个不同的船长，相隔数周，都在自己的数据流变成静电之前提到了同一星区的幽灵交通。其中一个截获到一个残缺的应答器信号，旧联殖格式，标号指向一艘本该封存的长程战斗舰。这不是你能耸肩带过的那种巧合。不管她在那外面做什么，她走在一条我们建成又掩埋的航线上，而下一步就落在一艘本不该出现在那里的死海军船上。

#en:
I am recording this from the dorm pod on BX-1113, lights dimmed, drive offline, ship humming that empty kind of quiet where you hear every relay breathe. We are not where the manifest says we should be. We are too far off the lane, too close to a cluster that never appears on the standard route projections, and no one is logging a deviation.  

I watched the senior techs argue over the nav console yesterday. Voices low, faces tight. One of them slid a datapad into their jacket when they noticed me in the reflection. Later, over reconstituted soup, they joked about "creative routing" and changed the subject so fast it left a pressure drop in the room.  

There are gaps in the records. Whole jump segments summarized in one clean line, no residual data, like the ship decided not to remember where it had been. I heard someone mention an old UC array out this way, a listening post that "does not exist anymore." That was followed by a long silence and a lot of looking at the ceiling.  

I am not stupid. First there was that job on the fringe rock where we found a slate full of corrupted corridor data. Then the scientist on the research module who kept asking if our routes ever passed close to abandoned military infrastructure. Now this ship, off-course, carrying ledgers no one wants audited. There is a pattern here. The parts everyone refuses to say out loud are the ones that scare me most.
zh:
我在 BX-1113 的住舱里录下这些，灯光调暗，驱动离线，飞船嗡嗡地响着那种空荡的安静，让你听得到每一个中继站在呼吸。我们不在清单说我们该在的地方。我们偏离航道太远，离一片从不出现在标准航路投影上的星团太近，而没人记录偏离。

昨天我看着资深技工们围着导航控制台争论。声音很低，脸色紧绷。其中一个在倒影里注意到我时，把一块数据板塞进了外套。后来就着复水汤，他们拿"创意航路"开玩笑，换话题换得飞快，房间里像留下了一道气压落差。

记录里有空白。整段整段的跃迁被一行干净的字概括，没有残留数据，像飞船决定不记得自己去过哪里。我听到有人提到这方向有一座旧联殖阵列，一座"已经不存在"的监听站。随后是长时间的沉默和大量盯着天花板的动作。

我不傻。先是外缘岩石上那份活，我们在那里找到一块满是损坏走廊数据的数据板。然后是研究模块上那位一直问我们航线有没有靠近过废弃军事基础设施的科学家。现在又是这艘偏离航道、载着没人想被审计的账簿的飞船。这里有一个图案。所有人都不肯说出口的那些部分，恰恰是最让我害怕的。

#en:
I am recording this from a bunk that smells like coolant and old socks, somewhere under the plating of the moonside relay. The broker is three doors down, pretending he is just a middleman, that the crates stacked in his bay are nobody's business but his. We both know that is a lie.

I ran diagnostics on his cargo feed under the excuse of checking for leaks. The route tags looked familiar in the wrong kind of way: same off-lane jumps, same quiet ports that somehow never appear in official traffic summaries. When I overlaid them with a copied harvest schedule from a frontier colony I worked last season, the pattern snapped into place. All those "anonymous" shipments pass through one dirtball farm that should have failed years ago.

The broker saw the plot come up on my slate. He glanced once, then looked away like we had both agreed not to say the name of the place out loud. No threats, no bargaining, just that shared understanding that some things stay between people who enjoy breathing. 

So now I know where the next piece lies, buried under glow-sick soil and old promises. Up to this point, all I had were rumors from a solitary homestead, a forgotten dataslate that should have been wiped, and the way certain cargo manifests kept looping back on themselves. Every new whisper has circled closer to the same man, the same routes, and that one farm sitting like a knot in the middle of it all.
zh:
我在一张闻着冷却液和旧袜子味的铺位上录下这些，位置在卫星背阴面中继站的某层甲板底下。经纪商就在三扇门之外，假装自己只是个中间人，假装他货位里堆着的箱子只是他自己的事。我们都知道那是谎话。

我借口查漏，对他的货物流数据跑了诊断。那些航路标签以一种不对的方式眼熟：同样偏离航道的跃迁，同样不知怎的从不出现在官方交通摘要里的安静港口。当我把它们和我上季度干过的一座外缘殖民地的收成表叠在一起时，图案啪地对上了。所有那些"匿名"货运都经过一座多年前本该倒闭的土球农场。

经纪商看见那块图在我数据板上弹出来。他瞟了一眼，然后移开目光，像我们俩都已默认不把那地方的名字说出口。没有威胁，没有讨价还价，只有那份共同的默契：有些事只留在还想活着呼吸的人之间。

所以现在我知道下一块碎片躺在哪儿了，埋在发光的病土和旧承诺底下。到目前为止，我手里只有来自一座孤零零农家院的传言、一块本该被擦掉却被遗忘的数据板，以及某些货运清单不断绕回自身的样子。每一声新的低语都更靠近同一个男人、同样的航线，以及那座像结一样坐在这一切中央的农场。
